intended_object: The universal property of the free (noncommutative) associative R-algebra on a set X. It is the natural bijection between functions X → A and R-algebra homomorphisms R⟨X⟩ → A, for any R-algebra A. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The forward map is `liftAux`, which extends f to an algebra homomorphism defined on the quotient of `Pre R X`. The inverse is precomposition with ι, so `F ↦ F ∘ ι`, as `lift_symm_apply` confirms. Being an equivalence encodes both existence and uniqueness of the lift, which is exactly the universal property.

The setting is the standard one for free associative algebras: R is a commutative semiring and A is any (not necessarily commutative) R-algebra over a semiring. Nothing narrower is assumed. This is Mathlib's own canonical definition of the notion, so there is no separate counterpart to cite.
